method.derivation: grounded-theory open coding on a 200-paper stratified sample, saturated at paradigm level by n~100
method.axis: 28-candidate seed (10 corpus-derived problems + 8 PI-named constructs + 10 scan constructs) merged abductively into 18 categories
method.naming: every paradigm, sub-paradigm and difficulty name is a term harvested from the corpus or supplied by the PI; zero analyst coinages

caveats: papers[] holds the 1,651 papers that were assigned a design paradigm. The other 97 of the 1,748-paper corpus were read and coded but fit no paradigm; they are in excluded_papers[] with reasons, not omitted. See meta.corpus_accounting. The 2 orphan PDFs (9767, 9769) both received a paradigm and are in papers[] with an empty url field, not in excluded_papers[].

Lifecycle stage assignment is the PI's, as given. lifecycle.proposed_adjustments holds 7 rows: 6 propose an evidence-backed change and 1 (P11) records that no change is needed. NONE are applied. lifecycle_adjusted.png renders 5 of the 6 — P13's is conditional (either/or, see its note) and was left unapplied.
Sub-paradigm v1.1 split proposals for P6/P8/P10/P11 are recorded but not applied.
Five difficulty names rest on 3-5 paper attestation and carry higher-frequency alternates.
F1 keeps the PI term "gulf of envisioning" though it appears in only 6 of its 415 papers; corpus alternative is "articulate" (105).
284 papers sit in per-paradigm tails below the sub-paradigm promotion bar; 219 of them carry cross-cutting patterns instead.

Sub-paradigm counts are per-paper assignments. Eight watch-list sub-paradigms differ from the original aggregate clustering (largest: P6 Structured Format 145->115, P10 Role-Playing Agent 40->59); both numbers are carried as n and n_aggregate_cluster. The per-paper count is authoritative and matches paper_rids.

proposed_adjustments.proposed_change: Split across stages: keep Likeness-of-a-Real-Individual (23) in 2.5 Personalization; move Assistant-as-Character (77) and Roleplay Counterpart (40) to 2.2 During AI working; move Population Surrogate Panel (26) to 2.3 Eval
proposed_adjustments.evidence: Only 23/183 (13%) of P10 is personalization in the conditioning sense. Top problems are H7 reciprocal feedback 27%, H6 motivation 19%, H8 skill rehearsal 18% — none is a personalization signature. The 4 sub-clusters come from the approved watch-list analysis (kappa 0.75).

proposed_adjustments.proposed_change: Add to 2.2 During AI working for the Implicit Signal Conditioning sub-cluster (35 papers); keep the other 212 in 2.1
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P6's Implicit Signal Conditioning harvests signals (gaze, speech features, learning-analytics data) at generation time rather than being set beforehand, so it is not context-setting in the elicitation sense.

P3 Context-Triggered Proactive Assistance n=124; H4 workflow interruption is its #2 problem at 20% (26 papers). Triggering on ambient context IS context acquisition — currently the only paradigm in 2.2 with no 2.1 membership despite 'Context-Triggered' in its name.

proposed_adjustments.paradigm_name: Pipeline of Stages with Iterative Refinement
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P5 n=310, the largest paradigm. H1 opacity is its #2 problem at 11% (37 papers) — inspectable intermediate stages are what the user watches DURING generation, not only what they steer afterwards.

proposed_adjustments.paradigm_name: Explanation and Verification of Generated Content
proposed_adjustments.proposed_change: Drop 2.2 During AI working, keep 2.3 only — OR keep both if in-generation self-check counts
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P13 n=67 is 55% H1 opacity, 19% H5 prediction blind spots. Verification overlays act on already-generated content; whether that is 'during' depends on whether streaming self-check counts as in-flight. Sam's call.
proposed_adjustments.note: Stated as either/or — depends on whether in-generation self-check counts as "during". Left at 2.2+2.3 in lifecycle_adjusted.png pending the PI's call.

proposed_adjustments.paradigm_name: Adaptive Interfaces from Inferred User State
proposed_adjustments.evidence: P15 n=29 is 31% H1 opacity, 13% H4 workflow interruption. Inferred-state adaptation happens continuously at runtime; the watch-list analysis kept it whole as 'Inferred-State Continuous Adaptation' — continuous means in-flight.
P11 n=37 is 35% H10 social friction. Its AI-Mediated Human Hand-Off sub-cluster (18) is turn-sequencing, which is both setup and follow-up. Assignment already reflects that.

F3.basis: Canonical judgment-and-decision-making construct; names the field the column sits in.

F5.basis: Lee & See, Human Factors 46(1) 2004, 'Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance', doi:10.1518/hfes.46.1.50_30392; Schemmer et al., IUI 2023, doi:10.1145/3581641.3584066. States the target rather than the failure, as the other columns do.

F9.basis: Attested in the column's own 218 papers: guid* in 72, feedback in 52, critique in only 5. One term per sub-factor - guidance for 'direction while stuck' (176), feedback for 'external critique' (54).

F11.basis: Nass & Moon, J. Soc. Issues 56(1) 2000, 'Machines and Mindlessness', doi:10.1111/0022-4537.00153; Davis 1989 (TAM). Its one sub-factor is 'acceptance and social perception of the agent'.

F13.basis: Kept as Personalization at the PI's direction. Note for the record: its sub-factors are engagement and immersion (291), motivation (94), behaviour change (56) and long-term adherence (46) - personalization is the remedy those papers apply, not the factor itself.

F16.basis: Edmondson, ASQ 44(2) 1999, doi:10.2307/2666999 (psychological safety); Malone & Crowston, ACM Comput. Surv. 1994 (coordination). Names both halves: coordination (73), minority voice and psychological safety (24), consensus (21).

F19.basis: Shortened from 'Effort, cognitive load and attention' for parallel structure; attention survives as a sub-factor (91).

F20.basis: Bandura 1977 (self-efficacy). Shortened from 'Skill, expertise and self-efficacy'; the expertise barrier survives as a sub-factor (385).

F21.basis: 184 of its papers are social sharing and human connection (128) and social presence and team rapport (56) - relational, not only emotional.

F22.basis: Unchanged in substance; Title Case for parallel structure.

notes: 1628 rows of design_patterns_papers.csv name 14 patterns that are absent from the 83-pattern source catalogue; they carry no id, category or definition and were dropped.
47 papers carry no v2 pattern: 37 appear nowhere in the pattern coding, and 10 had edges only to the dropped patterns above. They stay browsable and keep their factors.
85 pattern edges and 57 factor edges are low-confidence and are marked review_status=needs_review. They are published, not withheld.
The five factors new in v2 (N1-N5) have no factor-level definition in the source catalogue; their pages lead with sub-factor definitions instead.
Factor membership is a fresh coding pass, not a remap: only 49%% of the 4,394 factor edges in the 1.x data survive into v2, and the primary/secondary distinction no longer exists.
67 papers excluded as no-fit under the old taxonomy carry patterns in v2 and now appear in the catalogue.

Factor taxonomy revised editorially: 5 factors renamed (F3->Judging and deciding, F4->Oversight, F7->Control and agency, F11->Mindset, F15->Spatial and embodied cognition), 4 sub-factors reparented, F10 and N5 retired. 1 edges repointed and 30 dropped; renamed factors keep source_factor_name and are flagged definition_is_stale because their 1.x definition and boundary rule predate the v2 sub-factors.

Category ids were renumbered so U01-U10 runs in the site's reading order (its stages). Each category keeps its source id as source_category_id and the mapping is in migration.category_id_remap; pattern ids were not renumbered.
3 patterns were withdrawn on review — pat-008, pat-073, pat-084 — taking 7 paper edges with them. Their papers stay in the corpus, holding every other pattern and factor they carry.

Every pattern now carries a title; the clause it was named by in the source catalogue is kept verbatim as its description, and both are searchable. 10 factors were renamed against external anchors, 11 recased, and the five newest were renumbered from the N-series into F19-F22.

The reading order is 4 stages: Setting the context, Taking in the output, Acting on the output, Fitting into the work. "Working the output" was split, so a pattern's stage no longer follows from its category id alone.

U03.basis: 'Agency' collided with the F7 column, Control and Agency; a category and a factor sharing a word made the matrix ambiguous to read.

U04.basis: 'Output Rendering' was inaccurate for the category's own contents: pat-060 (multimodal input), pat-062 (voice as the input surface) and pat-061 (explicitly 'input or output') are not output rendering.

categories.category_description: How users, artifacts, examples, parameters, or user-state signals specify intent and shape the system's next behavior.
categories.classification_boundary: Requires a user-facing specification or adaptive interaction; invisible sensing infrastructure is excluded.

categories.category_description: When assistance appears and who triggers it: system-initiated, continuous, deferred, session-bound, or explicitly summoned.
categories.classification_boundary: The timing or trigger must be observable in the interaction; surface placement alone belongs to U09.

categories.category_description: Visible rules or boundaries that restrict generation, protect artifact regions, preserve privacy, or reserve part of the task for the user.
categories.classification_boundary: The constraint must be expressed through the interface or directly shape an observable interaction; invisible policies are excluded.

categories.category_description: How interaction crosses sensory, physical, spatial, embodied, or representational channels.
categories.classification_boundary: The channel, embodiment, or rendering must be the load-bearing interface mechanism.

categories.category_description: How multiple possibilities are presented, previewed, maintained, blended, or compared before commitment.
categories.classification_boundary: Requires a visible choice or comparison mechanism, not backend candidate-set processing alone.

categories.category_description: How users inspect, modify, scope, revise, accept, program, or interrupt generated work at the artifact level.
categories.classification_boundary: Centers user control during or after generation, including editable intermediate generators and representations.

categories.category_description: How evidence, internals, correspondence, quality, interpretations, and planned actions are represented for human judgment.
categories.classification_boundary: The representation must support understanding or verification, rather than merely render output into a usable medium.

categories.category_description: How visible stages, dialogue states, histories, task decompositions, and session boundaries organize progress over time.
categories.classification_boundary: The process structure must be exposed to users; hidden chains of model calls are excluded.

categories.category_description: How AI assistance is spatially composed with artifacts, panels, host tools, chat surfaces, presentation modes, and shared workspaces.
categories.classification_boundary: Use for visible surface placement and integration, not sensory modality or physical-space registration.

categories.category_description: How human and artificial participants are personified, assigned visible roles, coordinated, simulated, or represented to one another.
categories.classification_boundary: Identity or social organization must be user-facing; invisible multi-agent division of labor is excluded.

patterns.short_summary: The system holds a variable describing the user — mental state, intent, goal, emotion, skill level — and its current value selects among enumerated alternative behaviors: different strategies, presentation forms, or difficulty settings.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Adapts strategy or presentation to intent, emotion, skill, or goal.
patterns.definition: The system holds a variable describing the user — mental state, intent, goal, emotion, skill level — and its current value selects among enumerated alternative behaviors: different strategies, presentation forms, or difficulty settings. The same task content is routed through different branches depending on the value.
patterns.structural_signature: A discrete branch, lookup table, or mapping between a state variable and a fixed set of named alternative behaviors, evaluated before output is produced. The alternatives are enumerable and the mapping is authored at design time, so the behavior set is finite and the state variable is the only thing selecting among its members.
patterns.source_pattern_name: inferred or declared user state selects the system's next behavior
patterns.description: inferred or declared user state selects the system's next behavior

patterns.short_summary: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Structures specification as an elicitation dialogue rather than a single prompt.
patterns.definition: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from. The usual prompt-then-generate direction is inverted.
patterns.structural_signature: A system-authored question precedes any user content at the head of the loop, and each reply is written into the input record consumed by the next stage. The set of questions determines which slots of the specification exist, so the user never composes a full specification unprompted.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the system questions the user and the answers become the input
patterns.description: the system questions the user and the answers become the input

patterns.short_summary: Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Lets users communicate intent by showing desired behavior or outcomes.
patterns.definition: Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification. The supplied artifact is treated as a definition of desired behaviour, not merely as content to draw on. What the system produces from it — a template, a constraint graph, a set of control states, a reusable action — is what governs subsequent generation.
patterns.structural_signature: The input slot accepts finished exemplars; an induction step converts them into a reusable structure (template, constraint set, parameter assignment, recorded macro); that structure, and not the exemplars, is what conditions later runs and what the user can edit. Adding or removing exemplars changes the induced structure.
patterns.source_pattern_name: demonstration or example as the specification
patterns.description: demonstration or example as the specification

patterns.short_summary: The user states in language what they want to be true of the artifact, and the system performs the corresponding edit or retrieval.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Reframes interaction from procedural control to outcome-oriented conversation.
patterns.definition: The user states in language what they want to be true of the artifact, and the system performs the corresponding edit or retrieval. Language stands in for the direct-manipulation repertoire that would otherwise be used — selecting a function, adjusting a control, issuing a query. The substitution is the claim: the manipulation handles are not offered alongside.
patterns.structural_signature: The artifact has an established non-linguistic control vocabulary (transformation functions, palette editors, query forms, element handles). The interface exposes a text or utterance field as the operative control over that artifact, parses the utterance into the operation, and applies it; the user names an outcome rather than a procedure. The artifact itself remains a separate object from the language channel — the utterance is about it, not an entry in it.
patterns.source_pattern_name: natural-language instruction replaces direct manipulation of the artifact
patterns.description: natural-language instruction replaces direct manipulation of the artifact

patterns.short_summary: An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Makes existing user artifacts the contextual basis of generation.
patterns.definition: An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on. The user supplies material rather than a description of what they want. The output is a function of that material.
patterns.structural_signature: The system exposes an ingestion path for a user-owned artifact (upload, parse, encode, capture) and routes it into the generator as conditioning state, either directly or after an encoding step. The generation cannot run without that artifact; changing it changes the output. The material is pre-existing with respect to the interaction — it is not authored in order to specify the request.
patterns.source_pattern_name: generation conditioned on the user's own material
patterns.description: generation conditioned on the user's own material The user hands over material they already own - a dataset, PDF, photo set or chat log - and the generation is conditioned on it.

patterns.short_summary: Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Places a predictable prompt-action menu on every content item.
patterns.definition: Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds. Invoking one runs its prompt against that unit. The user's expressive choice is reduced to picking which of the fixed actions to apply and to which unit.
patterns.structural_signature: The content is partitioned into units; a fixed vocabulary of n named actions is defined once, system-wide; each unit exposes all n as invocable affordances, and invocation binds (action, unit) into a generation call. The action set does not vary by unit and is not editable by the user, so the interaction space is exactly units × actions. Transplants to any repository of units — a codebase with a fixed per-function action menu, a document set with a fixed per-section menu.
patterns.source_pattern_name: a fixed set of predefined prompts attached to each unit of content
patterns.description: a fixed set of predefined prompts attached to each unit of content The same small, named set of prepared AI actions is attached to every content unit, in place of an open prompt box.

patterns.short_summary: The system borrows the vocabulary of an already-known artifact — a spreadsheet, a paint palette, a plant, a social feed — and uses it wholesale as the surface through which the user acts, rather than devising controls specific to the underlying operation.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Builds the interface from the objects and actions of a known domain.
patterns.definition: The system borrows the vocabulary of an already-known artifact — a spreadsheet, a paint palette, a plant, a social feed — and uses it wholesale as the surface through which the user acts, rather than devising controls specific to the underlying operation. The borrowed source supplies both the visual encoding and the set of legal actions.
patterns.structural_signature: The interface presents the objects of a source domain external to the system and accepts that domain's operations as its input actions; each such action is translated into a system operation, so the two sets stand in one-to-one correspondence. What is on screen is the source domain's objects and their legal actions, whether or not the paper states the mapping.
patterns.source_pattern_name: familiar metaphor imported as the interaction surface
patterns.description: familiar metaphor imported as the interaction surface The interface is built from an object the user already knows - a spreadsheet, a palette, puzzle pieces, recipe cards.

patterns.short_summary: The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses canvas position, grouping, and connection as the specification surface.
patterns.definition: The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification. Proximity, grouping, and connections between elements determine what is generated, so moving an element changes the request. The canvas replaces a linear prompt field as the place where intent is expressed.
patterns.structural_signature: Elements are freely positionable on an unbounded surface; the system's input is derived from the configuration — coordinates, distances, containment, or explicit links — and not only from the elements' contents. Rearranging without changing any element's content still changes the system's output.
patterns.source_pattern_name: spatial arrangement on a canvas is the prompt
patterns.description: spatial arrangement on a canvas is the prompt

patterns.short_summary: A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Maps a persistent system property to an ordered control.
patterns.definition: A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance. Setting the value re-runs or re-renders under the new setting. The dimension exists before any particular content and persists across generations.
patterns.structural_signature: A named parameter with an ordered range (short/moderate/long; 1D distance; temperature; abstraction level) is surfaced as a persistent control widget bound to that range. The control does not create content; it scales an already-defined property of whatever content is produced, and the same control is available for every output. Multiple such parameters may be exposed together as a configuration panel.
patterns.source_pattern_name: a system or generation property exposed as a level the user sets
patterns.description: a system or generation property exposed as a level the user sets

patterns.short_summary: The user's freehand mark — a stroke, a scribble, an arrow, a drawn layout — is taken as input to generation, either alongside or in place of a written prompt.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses drawn geometry as a direct input channel.
patterns.definition: The user's freehand mark — a stroke, a scribble, an arrow, a drawn layout — is taken as input to generation, either alongside or in place of a written prompt. The mark's geometry and its position carry specification, not merely selection. Each drawing pass conditions the next generated result, so drawing is the steering channel.
patterns.structural_signature: A drawing surface captures freehand vector input; the captured strokes are passed to the generator as conditioning signal; the generated result is returned into or beside the same surface so it can be drawn on again. The stroke's shape and placement are consumed as content, so two different strokes in the same location yield different results.
patterns.source_pattern_name: sketch or drawn stroke as the generation input
patterns.description: sketch or drawn stroke as the generation input

patterns.short_summary: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Turns inferred concepts into editable chips, sliders, weights, or selections.
patterns.definition: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates. The user steers subsequent behaviour by editing, weighting, selecting or deselecting members of the extracted set rather than by rewriting free text. The set is content-specific: a different input yields a different set of handles.
patterns.structural_signature: A derivation step produces a finite list of named items from the current input; those items are rendered as individually addressable widgets (chips, rows, sliders, editable fields); manipulating them re-parameterizes the downstream operation. The handle set is regenerated when the input changes, so the control panel's contents are data-dependent rather than fixed at design time.
patterns.source_pattern_name: extracted keywords or attributes exposed as control handles
patterns.description: extracted keywords or attributes exposed as control handles

patterns.short_summary: The system emits its output in step with an activity that is unfolding independently — a conversation, a performance, a learning session, a walk through an environment — so that each output appears at the moment its referent occurs.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Defines real-time coordination between assistance and an unfolding activity.
patterns.definition: The system emits its output in step with an activity that is unfolding independently — a conversation, a performance, a learning session, a walk through an environment — so that each output appears at the moment its referent occurs. Timing is part of the design, not an implementation detail: an output delivered late would be the wrong output. The pattern is about when material is shown, not what it contains.
patterns.structural_signature: An input stream is consumed continuously and each produced item is scheduled against a timestamp in that stream; the pipeline is held to a latency budget so that the item is presented while its referent is still current. There is no batch boundary between the activity and the output — the activity does not have to end for output to appear.
patterns.source_pattern_name: output synchronized to the live activity as it happens
patterns.description: output synchronized to the live activity as it happens

patterns.short_summary: Rather than an always-on stream, the system packages interaction into episodes with a defined opening and close.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Defines the opening, closing, and continuity model of the experience.
patterns.definition: Rather than an always-on stream, the system packages interaction into episodes with a defined opening and close. Each session covers a bounded slice of material and ends; the next session is a new episode rather than a continuation of the same thread. The boundary is imposed by the system, not by the user walking away.
patterns.structural_signature: Control flow is a repeated cycle with an entry condition and a terminal state: material is admitted at session start, processed through a fixed internal flow, and the session closes, after which no further turns belong to it. Session boundaries are visible as flow-diagram endpoints and as scoping for what the system may reference. Transplants to any continuous process that could have been left running — monitoring, tutoring, journaling, review.
patterns.source_pattern_name: interaction bounded into discrete sessions rather than running continuously
patterns.description: interaction bounded into discrete sessions rather than running continuously

patterns.short_summary: Output is emitted without a user request immediately preceding it.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Defines proactive system initiative and the experience of unsolicited assistance.
patterns.definition: Output is emitted without a user request immediately preceding it. The trigger is a timer, a change in sensed or task state, or the system's own decision that intervention is warranted, and the user takes no action to summon what appears.
patterns.structural_signature: An output-producing edge in the control graph whose predecessor is not a user event: a clock, a state-change condition, or an internal decision step. There is no request object attributable to the user for that output, and the interface offers no control the user could have withheld to prevent it appearing at that moment.
patterns.source_pattern_name: system-initiated output with no user request
patterns.description: system-initiated output with no user request

patterns.short_summary: The system detects something during an ongoing activity but withholds any response until the activity has ended, then presents its findings and the user's controls in a dedicated step.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Defines a non-interruptive assistance strategy and delayed review phase.
patterns.definition: The system detects something during an ongoing activity but withholds any response until the activity has ended, then presents its findings and the user's controls in a dedicated step. The activity itself runs without system intrusion. The design choice is the placement in time, and the paper argues for it explicitly against the interrupting alternative.
patterns.structural_signature: Two phases: during phase one the system observes and accumulates without emitting anything to the user; on the terminating event of phase one, phase two opens with the accumulated findings and a set of controls that act retroactively on phase-one material. Nothing the system produces is visible before the boundary, and phase-two actions can revise what phase one produced. Transplants to editing, driving, code review, form filling — anywhere an assist could have fired mid-stream.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the intervention deferred to after the activity rather than interrupting it
patterns.description: the intervention deferred to after the activity rather than interrupting it

patterns.short_summary: A persistent region sits beside the surface the user is working on and shows generated content derived from that surface's current state.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Defines a persistent interface region that refreshes beside the artifact.
patterns.definition: A persistent region sits beside the surface the user is working on and shows generated content derived from that surface's current state. It refreshes on its own as the work changes rather than when the user asks. The panel is not the artifact under construction; it is a running commentary on it.
patterns.structural_signature: Two co-present regions with an asymmetric dependency: region A holds the user-authored state, region B renders a derived generation, and B is recomputed as a side effect of changes to A with no invocation step. B is typically read-only or non-committal — its content does not enter the artifact unless the user acts. The adjacency is spatial (margin, sidebar, docked panel) so that A and B are read together.
patterns.source_pattern_name: live-updating panel co-located with the working surface
patterns.description: live-updating panel co-located with the working surface

patterns.short_summary: A generated continuation is produced at the user's current position in the artifact being edited, and only when the user fires a control to ask for it.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Defines an inline invocation affordance and insertion point within the editor.
patterns.definition: A generated continuation is produced at the user's current position in the artifact being edited, and only when the user fires a control to ask for it. The user does not leave the editing surface to make the request or to receive the result.
patterns.structural_signature: A single user-triggered control whose output is inserted at the current insertion point of the same editable surface. There is no separate request window and no navigation step; when the control is not fired, nothing is generated, so the output's position and timing are both determined by the user's cursor and keystroke.
patterns.source_pattern_name: suggestion summoned on demand inside the working surface
patterns.description: suggestion summoned on demand inside the working surface

patterns.short_summary: The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Gives users persistent governance over future system behavior.
patterns.definition: The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run. Entries are authored by the user, usually in natural language, and the set is displayed as an inspectable, editable list. The set governs generation as a persistent policy rather than as a one-off instruction.
patterns.structural_signature: A named collection with add / edit / remove / reorder operations, persisted across generations and rendered as a list. Each entry originates from a user act (typed preference, feedback on an output converted into a rule, an imported written protocol) and is compiled into something the generator consults — a prompt fragment, an executable predicate, a decoding constraint, an ordering. Priority among entries may be expressed by position in the list rather than by numeric weight.
patterns.source_pattern_name: user-authored criteria or constraint set governing generation
patterns.description: user-authored criteria or constraint set governing generation

patterns.short_summary: The system runs the pipeline that would produce a terminal output but does not emit that output.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Preserves an essential cognitive or creative step for the person.
patterns.definition: The system runs the pipeline that would produce a terminal output but does not emit that output. What it emits instead is one step short — candidates, marked passages, correctness without the answer, questions — and the person supplies the missing final step.
patterns.structural_signature: The last stage of the pipeline is truncated at the presentation boundary: what reaches the screen is an intermediate of the process whose end product is withheld, and the interface exposes no control that reveals it. The user's action supplies the terminal value, so the loop cannot close without a human act.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the system withholds the answer and hands the step back to the user
patterns.description: the system withholds the answer and hands the step back to the user

patterns.short_summary: Part of the working artifact is designated off-limits and the generator is prevented from altering it, with the designation produced by the system rather than drawn by the user.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Establishes a preservation contract around existing user-authored material.
patterns.definition: Part of the working artifact is designated off-limits and the generator is prevented from altering it, with the designation produced by the system rather than drawn by the user. The user contributes the artifact and, implicitly, its already-authored parts; the system works out what must be preserved and enforces that during generation. Generation is thereby restricted to the complement of the protected set.
patterns.structural_signature: The artifact is partitioned into a protected subset and a mutable subset; the partition is computed (by segmentation, or by provenance of who authored each element) rather than selected; generation is then executed under a constraint or penalty that forbids modifying, overwriting or occluding the protected subset. Two things are needed and both are observable: an automatic partition step, and an enforcement mechanism at generation time. Transplants to text (generate around the user's own sentences), code (do not touch hand-written blocks), layout, audio.
patterns.source_pattern_name: regions the user did not mark protected from generation
patterns.description: regions the user did not mark protected from generation

patterns.pattern_name: Low Detail Outlines with User-Filled Specificity
patterns.short_summary: The system renders its output below the fidelity it could achieve, using a sparse representation and minimal accompanying text.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses intentionally unfinished presentation to invite user contribution.
patterns.definition: The system renders its output below the fidelity it could achieve, using a sparse representation and minimal accompanying text. The reduction is deliberate and stated as a design goal, not a technical limit. What is withheld — detail, finish, specificity — is what the user is expected to supply.
patterns.structural_signature: A ceiling is imposed on the rendering stage: outputs are emitted in a low-detail representation (outline instead of full render, one line instead of a paragraph) uniformly across all outputs, with no affordance to raise the fidelity. The invariant is that the representation underdetermines the artifact — many finished artifacts are consistent with what is shown. Transplants to wireframes instead of mockups, outlines instead of prose, thumbnails instead of masters.
patterns.source_pattern_name: output rendered at a fixed low fidelity with no higher-fidelity mode
patterns.description: output rendered at a fixed low fidelity with no higher-fidelity mode The user supplies the missing detail and specificity themselves.

patterns.short_summary: A structure declared in advance — a schema, slot set, section skeleton, or typed taxonomy — determines the form the model's output must take.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Presents generated output through predefined fields, sections, or structural slots.
patterns.definition: A structure declared in advance — a schema, slot set, section skeleton, or typed taxonomy — determines the form the model's output must take. Generation is validated against or rendered into that structure rather than emitted as free text. The structure exists at the type level: it applies to every output the system produces, not just this one.
patterns.structural_signature: A named structure with enumerated parts (fields, sections, component types, category labels) is defined independently of any single generation and is stored in the system. The generator's output is emitted into, checked against, or parsed by that structure, and downstream rendering is per-part: each part gets its own visual slot, colour, or handle. Outputs that do not conform are corrected or rejected before display.
patterns.source_pattern_name: schema or template constrains what the model may emit
patterns.description: schema or template constrains what the model may emit

patterns.short_summary: The agent is given a rendered body — an animated character, a 3-D figure, an on-screen avatar, a participant tile — and the user addresses that figure rather than a text pane.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Gives the agent a visible body, character, expression, or participant tile.
patterns.definition: The agent is given a rendered body — an animated character, a 3-D figure, an on-screen avatar, a participant tile — and the user addresses that figure rather than a text pane. The body is the locus of the agent's turns: speech, expression, or animation issue from it. Several papers treat embodiment as a graded design variable with the text pane as the low end.
patterns.structural_signature: A persistent visual figure with its own extent and position is rendered in the interface, and the system's outputs are attributed to and emitted from that figure rather than from an undifferentiated output region. The figure occupies a slot ordinarily held by a human participant (a tile, a seat, a character in a scene).
patterns.source_pattern_name: embodied character or avatar as the agent's form
patterns.description: embodied character or avatar as the agent's form

patterns.short_summary: At least one end of the interaction loop lives in matter rather than pixels: objects are grasped, moved, or posed to issue commands, or the system's output is delivered as physical motion, staged space, or a tangible arrangement.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses tangible objects, movement, or spatial arrangements as interface elements.
patterns.definition: At least one end of the interaction loop lives in matter rather than pixels: objects are grasped, moved, or posed to issue commands, or the system's output is delivered as physical motion, staged space, or a tangible arrangement. The screen is displaced from that end of the loop.
patterns.structural_signature: Either the sensed event that constitutes a command is a physical manipulation of an object or body in space, or the emitted result is actuation or placement in space with no rendered layer required. The interface's layout is described in room coordinates, zones, and objects rather than in windows and widgets.
patterns.source_pattern_name: physical objects and physical space as the input or output channel
patterns.description: physical objects and physical space as the input or output channel

patterns.short_summary: The user drives the system by speaking, and the spoken utterance occupies the slot that a typed prompt or a direct-manipulation action would otherwise occupy.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Makes speech the operative command or prompting channel.
patterns.definition: The user drives the system by speaking, and the spoken utterance occupies the slot that a typed prompt or a direct-manipulation action would otherwise occupy. The system's other controls may still exist, but the contributed interaction is that speech is the channel through which intent enters. Papers in this group either build voice as the sole authoring channel or interrogate what happens when voice is collapsed onto the text pipeline.
patterns.structural_signature: An audio-capture channel is the entry point of the control flow; the utterance is converted to an internal command, instruction sequence, or code, and that conversion product is what the rest of the system consumes. Nothing else in the flow requires the user to touch a pointer or keyboard, and the surface that would normally accept typed or pointed input is either absent or bypassed.
patterns.source_pattern_name: spoken channel as the interaction surface in place of typed input
patterns.description: spoken channel as the interaction surface in place of typed input

patterns.short_summary: One unit of system output is rendered in two or more sensory or representational channels at once — text plus speech, text plus image plus sound, or one language plus another.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Presents equivalent content through multiple sensory or representational channels.
patterns.definition: One unit of system output is rendered in two or more sensory or representational channels at once — text plus speech, text plus image plus sound, or one language plus another. The channels carry the same content rather than complementary content, so the user may take up whichever channel suits them. The duplication is deliberate and built into the generation or rendering step.
patterns.structural_signature: A single output item fans out to multiple renderers whose products are presented together (concurrently or in immediate succession), each renderer targeting a different channel. The channels are redundant with respect to content: removing one loses a way of receiving the item but not the item itself.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the same content delivered in more than one modality
patterns.description: the same content delivered in more than one modality

patterns.short_summary: Material that is not prose — extracted data, code, an algorithmic sequence, a probability, a structure — is converted into natural language and delivered in that form.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Turns non-prose information into a readable language surface.
patterns.definition: Material that is not prose — extracted data, code, an algorithmic sequence, a probability, a structure — is converted into natural language and delivered in that form. The prose is the output surface the user actually reads. The conversion is the design move: the same information was already available in a non-verbal form.
patterns.structural_signature: A non-prose source representation exists in the system, and a rendering step maps it to running natural language that is placed in the user-facing slot. The mapping is one-way and terminal: the prose is what the user consumes, and any downstream action is taken on the prose rather than on the source. The source may remain visible alongside, but the prose does not need to be re-parsed to be used.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the material rewritten as human-readable text
patterns.description: the material rewritten as human-readable text

patterns.short_summary: The model produces output in a representation the user cannot perceive directly — parameter streams, coordinate sequences, symbolic structures — and the system attaches a renderer that turns it into something viewable.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Adds a deterministic perceptual rendering for otherwise imperceptible output.
patterns.definition: The model produces output in a representation the user cannot perceive directly — parameter streams, coordinate sequences, symbolic structures — and the system attaches a renderer that turns it into something viewable. The rendering is not the model's output; it is a display layer chosen by the designer. The user judges the artifact only through that layer.
patterns.structural_signature: A rendering stage is inserted between generation and display: the generated representation R is mapped by a fixed, designer-chosen function into a perceptible form V, and only V appears in the interface. The mapping is deterministic and adds no content — everything shown is entailed by R plus fixed rendering assets. Where R is time-varying, V is commonly a sampled sequence laid out spatially. Transplants to sonifying a data stream, plotting a vector, animating a trajectory.
patterns.source_pattern_name: abstract output given a viewable rendered representation
patterns.description: abstract output given a viewable rendered representation

patterns.short_summary: Generated content is placed in the coordinate frame of a real scene, or of captured video of one, and attached to a referent within it rather than to a panel.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Anchors generated content to real-world referents.
patterns.definition: Generated content is placed in the coordinate frame of a real scene, or of captured video of one, and attached to a referent within it rather than to a panel. When the referent moves, the output moves with it.
patterns.structural_signature: Rendering requires a spatial resolution step: the system extracts positions of referents in the scene and lays out output at those coordinates, so an output element's location is a function of scene geometry rather than of a layout slot. Losing tracking loses placement, not content.
patterns.source_pattern_name: output spatially registered to the physical scene
patterns.description: output spatially registered to the physical scene

patterns.short_summary: Rather than reusing a standard chart type, the system introduces a new graphical mark whose geometry is designed around the specific property being communicated.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Creates a domain-specific graphical mark with explicit component-to-geometry mappings.
patterns.definition: Rather than reusing a standard chart type, the system introduces a new graphical mark whose geometry is designed around the specific property being communicated. The mark's parts each carry a distinct component of that property, and the mapping is defined by the paper. The encoding is a contributed object in its own right, described part by part.
patterns.structural_signature: A composite graphical mark is defined by an explicit mapping from named components of the data property to named geometric channels of the mark (sector angle, chord endpoint, block extent, static shape standing for a time-varying quantity). The definition is enumerable — the paper can label the parts — and the mark is instantiated once per unit of data. Transplantable in the sense that any property with named components can be given such a mark; but note that what is shared across instances is the *act of designing* a mark, and the marks themselves have nothing structural in common beyond compositeness.
patterns.source_pattern_name: a composite glyph whose parts each encode a named component of one property
patterns.description: a composite glyph whose parts each encode a named component of one property A purpose-built graphical mark rather than a standard chart type.

patterns.short_summary: Two or more physically distinct input channels — typed text, drawn marks, speech, pointing, body pose, GUI controls — are accepted for the same operation.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Combines or interchanges text, speech, drawing, pointing, pose, and GUI input.
patterns.definition: Two or more physically distinct input channels — typed text, drawn marks, speech, pointing, body pose, GUI controls — are accepted for the same operation. They are either fused into one request or freely interchangeable within a single interaction, without a mode change.
patterns.structural_signature: The input side of one operation has at least two capture channels feeding a single request object, and the system must fuse or arbitrate between them. The user can switch channels mid-operation without transitioning the interface to a different state, so channel choice is not a mode.
patterns.source_pattern_name: multiple input modalities and gestures accepted together
patterns.description: multiple input modalities and gestures accepted together

patterns.short_summary: A structured artifact is exposed as a traversable graph of positions that the user steps through with discrete commands, with the system's response delivered on a nonvisual channel.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Supports traversal of structured content using nonvisual commands and positional feedback.
patterns.definition: A structured artifact is exposed as a traversable graph of positions that the user steps through with discrete commands, with the system's response delivered on a nonvisual channel. Position within the structure is announced, so the user's location is part of the output rather than something read off a display. The artifact is not flattened into a single linear description.
patterns.structural_signature: The artifact is parsed into addressable nodes (items, points, layers, regions); the input surface is a small set of discrete move commands (next, previous, into, out of) plus queries; each move emits a nonvisual rendering of the node reached together with an orientation cue naming where in the structure that node sits. The load-bearing property is the *persistent cursor*: state is carried between commands so the same key means different things at different positions. Transplants to any structured content and any nonvisual channel — a directory tree read aloud, a menu stepped through by haptics.
patterns.source_pattern_name: nonvisual sequential navigation through structure
patterns.description: nonvisual sequential navigation through structure

patterns.short_summary: A chain of generative transformations is placed inside the user's perceptual path, so that what the user perceives is the pipeline's reconstruction rather than the captured signal.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Makes a generative reconstruction the user's continuous perceptual surface.
patterns.definition: A chain of generative transformations is placed inside the user's perceptual path, so that what the user perceives is the pipeline's reconstruction rather than the captured signal. The original signal is not shown alongside; it is displaced, and the mediation is continuous and unavoidable while the system is worn or running. The category covers both readings of that arrangement: the plain control-flow case, where the pipeline simply sits between the scene and the display; and the case where the arrangement exists so that a property of the model is conveyed by making the user *undergo* its effects on their own perception rather than by describing, plotting or explaining it. Where a paper states only the experiential purpose, the interposed pipeline is still what is coded.
patterns.structural_signature: Capture → transform₁ → … → transformₙ → display, wired in series with no bypass: the sensor's output never reaches the display directly, and the display shows only the terminal transform's output. The chain typically crosses representations (signal → symbolic → signal), and the loss at each crossing is what the user perceives. Transplants to audio (mic → transcript → resynthesis → earpiece), text streams, or any sensed-and-displayed channel. For the experiential reading the same wiring holds, with one additional negative residue: no explanatory or visualization element for the model property being conveyed appears anywhere in the interface.
patterns.source_pattern_name: a generative pipeline interposed between the scene and the user's view
patterns.description: a generative pipeline interposed between the scene and the user's view What the user perceives is the pipeline's output rather than the scene itself.

patterns.short_summary: The user hands a whole multi-step task to the system through a non-visual act and then stops attending to it; there is no display at any point in the loop.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses a nonvisual handoff as the complete interface to a multi-step task.
patterns.definition: The user hands a whole multi-step task to the system through a non-visual act and then stops attending to it; there is no display at any point in the loop. Nothing is shown during execution, and the user cannot inspect progress. The handoff is complete at the moment of the request.
patterns.structural_signature: The interaction consists of an initiation gesture, a specification uttered on a non-visual channel, and a terminating signal, with no display surface in the loop and no intermediate state exposed. Structurally this forbids monitoring, mid-flight correction, and selection among alternatives: the control flow has exactly one user decision point, at the start. Transplants to any delegation without a display — a button on a wearable, a voice command to an appliance.
patterns.source_pattern_name: screenless task delegation with no visual interface
patterns.description: screenless task delegation with no visual interface

patterns.short_summary: The interface puts the system's assessment next to the user's own assessment of the same thing, so the two can be read against each other.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Structures reflection by having users compare committed human and AI assessments.
patterns.definition: The interface puts the system's assessment next to the user's own assessment of the same thing, so the two can be read against each other. Typically the user commits to a position first and the model's position is then revealed, with a further step in which the user may revise. The juxtaposition, and the divergence it exposes, is the designed object.
patterns.structural_signature: Two verdicts over the same item are held in the interface — one produced by the user, one by the system — and are displayed in the same view or in a fixed temporal order (user commits, system reveals, user re-decides). A revision affordance follows the reveal, and the difference between the two verdicts is itself rendered or computed.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the model's judgment placed alongside the person's own
patterns.description: the model's judgment placed alongside the person's own

patterns.short_summary: A checkpoint is interposed between composing content and transmitting it, at which the outgoing payload is displayed to the user together with the system's assessment of it.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Inserts a deliberate review and correction checkpoint before transmission.
patterns.definition: A checkpoint is interposed between composing content and transmitting it, at which the outgoing payload is displayed to the user together with the system's assessment of it. The user can edit, redact, or abstract before the content crosses the boundary. The design commitment is that the intervention is visible and happens on the user's side of the transmission.
patterns.structural_signature: Transmission is gated by a review state in which the exact payload is rendered, annotated with system-computed marks or scores, and made editable; the send proceeds only from that state, and edits made there change what is transmitted. The processing that produces the annotation runs before the boundary crossing, so the gate is client-side with respect to the recipient.
patterns.source_pattern_name: pre-send inspection of what is about to leave
patterns.description: pre-send inspection of what is about to leave

patterns.short_summary: The pipeline from input to output passes through a named intermediate artifact that is rendered for the user to read.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Renders an intermediate artifact for reading or editing before final output.
patterns.definition: The pipeline from input to output passes through a named intermediate artifact that is rendered for the user to read. That intermediate — a sentence, a block of code, a set of extracted entities, a prompt — is the object the user inspects and often edits, and the final output is produced from it. The mediation is deliberate: the system refuses to map input straight to output.
patterns.structural_signature: Between the user's input and the delivered artifact sits at least one representation that is (a) materialized as a distinct object in the system, (b) displayed in a human-readable form, and (c) actually consumed by the next stage to produce the output. Editing or rejecting the intermediate changes the output; the output cannot be produced without passing through it. Some members of this cluster are load-bearing on inspectability alone (the human reads the intermediate and makes the decision) rather than on editability.
patterns.source_pattern_name: inspectable intermediate representation between input and output
patterns.description: inspectable intermediate representation between input and output

patterns.short_summary: The system marks particular locations inside the user's content and attaches a deeper layer of material to each mark that is not shown until the user asks for it.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Combines lightweight inline indicators with expandable detail.
patterns.definition: The system marks particular locations inside the user's content and attaches a deeper layer of material to each mark that is not shown until the user asks for it. The first layer is a lightweight in-content indicator; the second is an expandable panel, popup, or tab bar holding explanation, alternatives, or scores. Detail is thus staged rather than presented all at once.
patterns.structural_signature: Per-unit annotations are rendered inline at their source location; each annotation is an interactive trigger (hover, click, expand) that opens a secondary container holding additional per-unit material. Collapsing the container returns the display to the marked-but-undetailed state, so the content view never carries the full detail at rest.
patterns.source_pattern_name: flagged spans highlighted in place with detail revealed on demand
patterns.description: flagged spans highlighted in place with detail revealed on demand

patterns.short_summary: Every unit of displayed content — a word, line, span, or segment — carries a value on some attribute, and that value is rendered by altering the appearance of the unit in place: colour, opacity, weight.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses styling to encode values directly on content units.
patterns.definition: Every unit of displayed content — a word, line, span, or segment — carries a value on some attribute, and that value is rendered by altering the appearance of the unit in place: colour, opacity, weight. The attribute is read off the content itself rather than from a separate annotation layer or panel.
patterns.structural_signature: A one-to-one map from content units to attribute values, rendered as a visual variable of each unit; the content's text, order, and layout are unchanged, so stripping the encoding restores the original artifact exactly. The display allocates no separate region to the attribute, and the number of encoded marks equals the number of content units.
patterns.source_pattern_name: a per-unit attribute encoded by colour or typography in the content itself
patterns.description: a per-unit attribute encoded by colour or typography in the content itself

patterns.short_summary: Many underlying events or measurements are collapsed into one number on a fixed scale, and that number is the interface's headline element.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Compresses underlying evidence into a bounded headline value.
patterns.definition: Many underlying events or measurements are collapsed into one number on a fixed scale, and that number is the interface's headline element. The score stands in for the history that produced it; the individual contributions are not the readout. Its bounded range gives the user a position rather than a raw quantity.
patterns.structural_signature: An accumulator over a stream of events is displayed as one scalar on a declared bounded interval, occupying a persistent, prominent slot in the layout. Structurally: many-to-one reduction, fixed range, single display element, updated as events arrive. No per-event breakdown is required for the pattern to hold, and the reduction function is the system's, not the user's. Transplants to any domain that scores a stream — a credit-style rating, a code-health number, a fitness ring.
patterns.source_pattern_name: a single aggregate score as the summary readout
patterns.description: a single aggregate score as the summary readout That single number is the interface's headline element.

patterns.short_summary: The system displays its own reading of what the user supplied — the construal, the inferred intent, the context it thinks it is in — as a first-class object rather than only acting on it.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Makes inferred intent or context visible and potentially correctable.
patterns.definition: The system displays its own reading of what the user supplied — the construal, the inferred intent, the context it thinks it is in — as a first-class object rather than only acting on it. The user can therefore see where the system's understanding diverges from their own, and in several cases can edit that understanding directly. The displayed object stands between the user's input and whatever the system produces next.
patterns.structural_signature: An inference step over the user's input emits a named artifact (graph, keyword overlay, natural-language restatement, schema instance) that is rendered persistently on screen; downstream behaviour is conditioned on that artifact. Where the artifact is editable, edits to it — not to the original input — are the channel by which the user corrects the system.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the model's interpretation of the input externalized on screen
patterns.description: the model's interpretation of the input externalized on screen

patterns.short_summary: The same collection is presented at more than one level of granularity, from an aggregate summary down to a single item.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Provides navigation across levels of granularity.
patterns.definition: The same collection is presented at more than one level of granularity, from an aggregate summary down to a single item. Interaction at a coarser level selects the population shown at the finer level. The finest level exposes the individual case behind the aggregate.
patterns.structural_signature: A hierarchy of at least two views over one collection, ordered by an aggregation relation: the coarse view displays a function of many items, the fine view displays items themselves. A selection in the coarse view is a filter that defines the fine view's contents, and the levels are simultaneously present or one-click reachable. The ordering is asymmetric — the fine level cannot substitute for the coarse one.
patterns.source_pattern_name: drill-down from aggregate overview to individual instance
patterns.description: drill-down from aggregate overview to individual instance

patterns.short_summary: A large collection of items is projected into a two-dimensional layout, and that layout — not a list, not a feed — is the primary surface the user navigates.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses a two-dimensional similarity layout as the primary exploration interface.
patterns.definition: A large collection of items is projected into a two-dimensional layout, and that layout — not a list, not a feed — is the primary surface the user navigates. Position encodes relatedness computed by the system, so proximity is meaningful. Queries and selections act on the map by re-weighting or re-highlighting it rather than by returning a separate result list.
patterns.structural_signature: A layout algorithm assigns each item a position in a shared 2-D space from a computed similarity or relation structure; the resulting arrangement is rendered as a pannable/zoomable canvas that is the main navigation control. Interaction operates on positions and neighbourhoods, and any query result is expressed as a change to the map's state rather than as a new view.
patterns.source_pattern_name: corpus laid out as a spatial map as the browse surface
patterns.description: corpus laid out as a spatial map as the browse surface Items are projected into a two-dimensional layout, and that layout is the browse surface rather than a list.

patterns.short_summary: Two or more display regions show the same underlying items under different encodings, and a correspondence between them is maintained and made visible.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Coordinates multiple representations through visible correspondence.
patterns.definition: Two or more display regions show the same underlying items under different encodings, and a correspondence between them is maintained and made visible. Acting on an element in one region changes the rendering of its counterpart in the others. The correspondence is the interface's claim: nothing shown in one view is orphaned from its counterpart elsewhere.
patterns.structural_signature: A set of items has more than one simultaneous rendering, and the system holds an identity mapping between renderings. A selection, brush, or hover event in region A triggers a rendering change (highlight, filter, scroll, annotation) on the mapped elements in region B, with the mapping stable across interactions. As clustered, the category also contains members where the correspondence is a fixed link from an output element to its source span rather than an interactive coordination — see the review flag.
patterns.source_pattern_name: linked views where selecting one element highlights its counterpart
patterns.description: linked views where selecting one element highlights its counterpart

patterns.short_summary: Before acting, the system displays the sequence of actions it intends to take, and that display persists as the actions are carried out.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Presents intended actions as a persistent plan, diagram, or step list.
patterns.definition: Before acting, the system displays the sequence of actions it intends to take, and that display persists as the actions are carried out. The plan is a visible object with its own structure — a diagram, a step list, a lookahead lane — and in several systems it is editable, so the user can alter the plan rather than react to its results. Commitment status may be encoded so the user can tell which parts are still revisable.
patterns.structural_signature: A planning step emits an ordered structure of forthcoming operations that is rendered before any of them executes; execution then advances through that structure while it remains on screen. Where the structure is editable, edits to unexecuted elements change what will run; visual encoding distinguishes executed, committed, and still-provisional elements.
patterns.source_pattern_name: the agent's plan rendered on screen before execution
patterns.description: the agent's plan rendered on screen before execution

patterns.short_summary: Quantities from inside the computation — attention weights, token or answer ranks, per-head importance, the spans the model relied on — are surfaced as a view the user can read and manipulate.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Visualizes attention, rankings, relied-upon spans, or other computational quantities.
patterns.definition: Quantities from inside the computation — attention weights, token or answer ranks, per-head importance, the spans the model relied on — are surfaced as a view the user can read and manipulate. What is displayed is not the output but the machinery that produced it. The view supports operations over those quantities, such as ranking, pruning, or comparing them.
patterns.structural_signature: The display is bound to intermediate values captured during inference rather than to the emitted result; those values are aggregated or projected into a view with its own controls (metric selectors, per-unit comparison, ablation toggles). Changing a control re-derives the view from the same captured values without re-running the user's task.
patterns.source_pattern_name: model internals rendered as an inspectable view
patterns.description: model internals rendered as an inspectable view

patterns.short_summary: Alongside an output, the system displays information about how that output came about: the derivation of a score, a confidence value, an uncertainty estimate, a quality diagnosis, or the agent's own stated reasoning.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Places provenance, confidence, uncertainty, or reasoning beside an output.
patterns.definition: Alongside an output, the system displays information about how that output came about: the derivation of a score, a confidence value, an uncertainty estimate, a quality diagnosis, or the agent's own stated reasoning. The disclosure adds no new task content.
patterns.structural_signature: A secondary display element bound one-to-one to a primary output element, carrying process metadata rather than task content. Its content is produced by or read from the producing pipeline, not from the user's material; removing it leaves the output intact and the task still performable.
patterns.source_pattern_name: disclosure of how the output was produced
patterns.description: disclosure of how the output was produced

patterns.short_summary: The interaction is organized as a tree or open graph in which alternatives coexist, rather than as a single ordered track the user advances along.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Supports forking, revisiting, and switching among persistent paths.
patterns.definition: The interaction is organized as a tree or open graph in which alternatives coexist, rather than as a single ordered track the user advances along. The user can fork off a side path, pick a different branch, or take steps in an order of their choosing, and the alternatives remain live rather than being replaced. The branching structure is often itself the interface object.
patterns.structural_signature: State is held as multiple simultaneously extant paths from a shared origin; a control exists for creating a new path and for switching which path is active; paths are displayed together (as a tree, a canvas of branches, or parallel panels) so their coexistence is visible. Advancing along one path does not destroy the others.
patterns.source_pattern_name: branching or freely-ordered structure instead of a linear sequence
patterns.description: branching or freely-ordered structure instead of a linear sequence

patterns.short_summary: The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Structures exploration as a controlled counterfactual test followed by comparison.
patterns.definition: The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one. The alteration is authored or parameterized by the user, and its known content is what makes the resulting difference readable. The comparison, not either output alone, is the thing the user is given.
patterns.structural_signature: Control flow: for a held input x, the system constructs one or more variants x' by a user-specified transformation rule (granularity, target, magnitude), executes the same model on x and each x', and joins the outputs into a paired or batched display keyed to the transformation that produced each. The distinguishing structure is that the delta is *induced by the interface* rather than found in the data, so the manipulated dimension is known to the system and can be used as the organizing axis of the display. This transplants: the same signature describes a spreadsheet what-if sweep, a compiler flag sweep, or an injected-decoy audit of a retrieval index.
patterns.source_pattern_name: perturb-then-compare probing of the model
patterns.description: perturb-then-compare probing of the model

patterns.short_summary: Two or more instances of the same kind of artifact are displayed simultaneously in parallel regions so that their differences can be read off directly.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Uses aligned parallel regions to make differences directly readable.
patterns.definition: Two or more instances of the same kind of artifact are displayed simultaneously in parallel regions so that their differences can be read off directly. The layout is the mechanism: nothing is computed for the user beyond alignment and co-presence. Which instances occupy the slots may itself be user-selectable.
patterns.structural_signature: Two or more renderings of comparable objects occupy spatially parallel regions at the same time, with corresponding parts aligned across regions. The comparison quantity is the visual difference between regions, and the display may add a diff encoding over the alignment. Slot assignment is a user action ("select any two…") or a fixed before/after pairing.
patterns.source_pattern_name: two artifacts placed side by side for comparison
patterns.description: two artifacts placed side by side for comparison

patterns.short_summary: A single user request is dispatched unchanged to several distinct models at once, and their outputs are returned together.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Presents attributed outputs from multiple models in a shared comparison frame.
patterns.definition: A single user request is dispatched unchanged to several distinct models at once, and their outputs are returned together. The variation the user sees comes from the difference between generators rather than from sampling one generator repeatedly. The outputs are attributable to their sources and set against each other.
patterns.structural_signature: Fan-out control flow: one input, n parallel invocations differing only in which backend is called, n outputs collected and presented in a common frame with source attribution. The key structural fact is that the *generator* is the varied dimension while the input is held constant — the inverse of perturbation probing. Transplants to any plural-backend setting: several solvers, several translation engines, several search indices.
patterns.source_pattern_name: one prompt fanned out to several models in parallel
patterns.description: one prompt fanned out to several models in parallel

patterns.short_summary: At a single decision point the system emits more than one alternative for the same request and presents them together as a set.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Presents a visible choice set at a single decision point.
patterns.definition: At a single decision point the system emits more than one alternative for the same request and presents them together as a set. The user's control is exercised by choosing one member of the set rather than by editing or re-specifying. The chosen item is committed downstream and the unchosen ones are discarded or backgrounded.
patterns.structural_signature: Control flow forks at one point into N ≥ 2 outputs of the same type, all rendered simultaneously in a bounded display region (a row, a side-by-side triple, a separate list beside the working surface). A selection event on one member is the commit action: it writes that member into the downstream state and terminates the other branches. The multiplicity is in the outputs, not in the operations offered over one output, and the set is resolved in a single act.
patterns.source_pattern_name: generated candidates offered for the user to pick among
patterns.description: generated candidates offered for the user to pick among

patterns.short_summary: The user selects two or more existing items and invokes an operation whose product is a single fused result rather than either operand.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Provides a manipulation for visibly combining source artifacts into a new output.
patterns.definition: The user selects two or more existing items and invokes an operation whose product is a single fused result rather than either operand. The blend may be continuous (interpolation along a mixing control) or discrete (a synthesized recombination). The operands remain identifiable as the things being combined, and the fusion is the system's contribution.
patterns.structural_signature: An operator takes two or more selected items as arguments and returns a result in the same space as the arguments; where the mixing is continuous, a control exposes the position between operands. Selecting the operands and invoking the operator are separate acts, and the result can itself become an operand.
patterns.source_pattern_name: two inputs blended or interpolated into one result
patterns.description: two inputs blended or interpolated into one result

patterns.short_summary: A process that would otherwise run to completion is made interruptible: the user can halt it, change its parameters while it continues, or leave it before it ends.
patterns.ui_ux_rationale: Gives users ongoing agency over a non-atomic process.
patterns.definition: A process that would otherwise run to completion is made interruptible: the user can halt it, change its parameters while it continues, or leave it before it ends. The intervention lands during execution, not before it starts or after it returns. The unit of generation or simulation is thereby made non-atomic.
