When several people judge the same material, papers treat both their convergence and their non-convergence as things at stake: agreement is wanted, but agreement reached by influence rather than independent assessment is a loss. The factor is this two-sided tension over how much judges should move toward each other. It transplants to any setting where multiple people rate, label, or decide on shared items.

factors.definition: People read a non-human counterpart in social terms — as warm or cold, competent or not, natural or stilted, a tool or an actor — and that reading governs whether they will have it around at all. The factor is the stance the person brings to the system, and the acceptance or refusal that follows from it.
factors.boundary_rule: Concerns the person's attitude toward the system as a social actor. F21 concerns their felt state and their connection to other people. Nearest sibling: F21 (Affect, Wellbeing and Connection).

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: acceptance and social perception of the agent
sub_factors.definition: People read a non-human counterpart in social terms — as warm or cold, competent or not, natural or stilted, a tool or an actor — and those readings govern whether they will have it around at all. Papers claim their designs engage this social attribution and the acceptance that follows from it. The dimension is the person's perceptual and attitudinal stance toward the counterpart, not their willingness to act on its outputs.
sub_factors.framing: BOTH — the corpus reports perceived anthropomorphism, warmth, and competence as dimensions to be raised, and robotic, unnatural, or discomforting impressions as the deficit designs address.

factors.definition: The person cannot tell or control what of theirs is visible to others — privacy of personal data and likeness on one side, ownership of their own contribution to a joint artifact on the other. Both are a loss of control over how the person is represented to others.
factors.boundary_rule: Concerns control over representation and attribution; F16 concerns the conduct of the shared activity itself. Nearest sibling: F16 (Coordination and Equitable Participation).

sub_factors.definition: The person's act of putting inner states, interpretations, or personal experience into an externalised form for others or for themselves. Papers claim their designs engage the reach and depth of that act — whether the person manages to convey what they meant, and how they feel about having disclosed it. The factor is the expressive act and its subjective adequacy, not the quality of the resulting artifact.
sub_factors.framing: CAPACITY — the corpus presents expression and disclosure as human activities to be enabled or deepened (emotional expression, satisfaction with one's disclosure, expressing an interpretation), with vulnerability noted alongside rather than as the dominant framing.

sub_factors.definition: The person's worry about what of themselves they are giving away, and the tendency to reveal more than the task requires. Papers frame the difficulty as decisions that are numerous, context-dependent, and made without perceptible control over the trade-off between usefulness and exposure. The factor is the person's concern and disclosure behaviour, not any confidentiality property of the technology.
sub_factors.framing: BOTH. Predominantly a harm (over-disclosure, privacy concerns, being overwhelmed by the volume of decisions), with a paired capacity framing in claims about perceptible control, consent as a dynamic process, and data sovereignty.

sub_factors.definition: Whether a person regards a result as theirs — as something they made and deserve credit for — when an intermediary did part of the making. Papers claim their designs engage this felt authorship and the credit that attaches to it. The question is attribution and possession of the result, not how much of the process the person directed.
sub_factors.framing: BOTH — the corpus names declines in ownership and self-credit as harms, and a strengthened sense of authorship or directorial agency as a capacity designs engage.

sub_factors.definition: A person must assemble and put forward an account of who they are for others to read, and doing so is a construction task distinct from having the qualities being presented. The factor is that work of building and expressing a professional or personal identity to an audience. It concerns the presented self, whatever the medium in which it is presented.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: preservation of the person's own voice and expression
sub_factors.definition: A person's distinctive style, intention, or way of speaking can be flattened or suppressed when an intermediary reshapes what they produce. Papers claim their designs engage the survival of that individual character through the intermediary's involvement. What is at stake is the particularity of this person's expression, not who is credited for the result.
sub_factors.framing: DEFICIT/HARM — the corpus states this as loss: intention and voice only partially captured, personal characteristics displaced by generic output, self-censorship, and cultural norms locked in place by filtering.

sub_factors.definition: An action that works perfectly well in private becomes costly when bystanders can see or hear it, and the person declines to perform it rather than be seen doing so. The factor is this social cost of visible or audible interaction in the presence of others, and the resulting unavailability of otherwise workable ways of acting. It concerns how the person is perceived by others nearby, not what the others learn.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: originality and appropriation of existing work
sub_factors.definition: What a person produces with help may reproduce someone else's work or manner without their knowing it, exposing them to a charge they did not intend to incur. The factor is the person's exposure to and concern about unoriginality — recreating prior art, taking on another's style, or plagiarism — as a property of the work they will put their name to. It concerns the relation between the person's output and other people's existing work.

factors.definition: Content or interaction pitched at no one in particular fails to connect with this person's situation, identity, or goals, and they disengage over time. The difficulty is the absence of personalization, and it is felt as drop-off rather than as error.
factors.boundary_rule: Is about material that does not fit this person, and the engagement that falls away as a result. F11 is about the stance the person takes toward the system as a social actor. Nearest sibling: F11 (Social Perception (Mindset)).

sub_factors.definition: How far a person is drawn into and absorbed by an experience rather than receiving it passively — engagement, immersion, presence, or felt involvement in the moment. Papers claim designs engage this by making the person an active participant or by deepening the sense of being inside the experience. It concerns absorption during the activity, not whether the person chose to start it or liked it afterwards.
sub_factors.framing: CAPACITY. Framed as something to foster, enhance, or evaluate — engagement, satisfaction and immersion, perceived presence, affective attachment.

sub_factors.definition: Whether a person wants to undertake and keep at an activity, and what they are pursuing through it. Papers claim their designs engage the drive to start and persist, including the underlying needs — autonomy, competence, relatedness — from which papers say that drive comes, and the mismatch when an activity's stated purpose is not the person's own. The factor is the wanting, prior to any question of ability.
sub_factors.framing: CAPACITY — the corpus states motivation as something to strengthen or raise: intrinsic motivation, intentions to practise, and the needs underpinning them.

sub_factors.definition: A person wants to conduct themselves differently from how they currently do, and cannot sustain the change against habit, ambivalence, and the states that drive the old conduct. Papers claim their designs engage both the entrenched pattern and the effort to move away from it. The object is the person's habitual conduct in life, not their use of the system in front of them.
sub_factors.framing: BOTH — the corpus names problematic, excessive, or mindless conduct as a harm the person themselves recognises, and behaviour change, perseverance, and mindfulness as capacities the design engages.

sub_factors.definition: Whether a person keeps coming back over weeks or months, when the benefit of an activity depends on repetition and the default trajectory is dropping off. The claimed difficulty is decline over time rather than the person's first encounter. It transplants to any activity whose value is only realized through sustained repeated participation.

factors.definition: The person's felt state in and around the activity: whether it lands as enjoyable or flat, the affective cost of engaging with heavy material, the stress they carry and how they cope with it, and their connection to other people — the sharing, co-presence and authenticity of exchange whose absence is felt as isolation.
factors.boundary_rule: Concerns how the person feels, and whom they feel it with. F11 concerns the stance they take toward the system itself. Nearest sibling: F11 (Social Perception (Mindset)).

sub_factors.definition: The felt quality of the experience for the person — whether it lands as enjoyable, moving, visceral, or by contrast as flat and desensitized. Papers claim the design engages the affective register of the encounter itself, not the person's task outcome. It transplants to any artifact whose worth is stated partly in how it feels to receive it.

The affective cost a person bears from being exposed to, or having to engage with, emotionally heavy material or events. Papers frame this as distress, overwhelm, frustration, vulnerability, or emotional harm that accumulates on the person and can drive them out of the activity. It transplants to any setting where sustained emotional exposure is part of the work or the encounter.

The person is under a stressor they experience as taxing, and the factor covers both the felt stress itself and their capacity to appraise and cope with it. Papers claim to engage the stressor, the appraisal, the coping response, or the person's sense of control over a situation they cannot structurally change. Transplants to any setting where a person must carry on under demand they did not choose.

Bonds between people are formed and maintained by sharing experience and being together in an activity, and their absence is felt as loneliness or isolation. Papers claim their designs engage this connection between people and the conditions that block or enable it. The relationship in question is human-to-human, even where a machine sits in the middle.
sub_factors.framing: BOTH — the corpus names connection, comfort, companionship, and shared creative engagement as goods, and loneliness and barriers to shared participation as the deficits designs address.

sub_factors.definition: The sense of being with other people, and the warmth, mutual awareness, and shared identity that build up between them. Papers frame the deficit as fragile early interaction, missing nonverbal cues, or an interface that pulls attention away from the group. It transplants to any mediated setting where people must feel co-present with one another to work or relate.

When part of what passes between two people was produced by something other than either of them, the exchange's standing as a genuine one comes into question — for the sender, the receiver, and the relationship. The factor is this concern about whether a mediated interaction still counts as authentic, and the reluctance or damage that attends it. It is a property of the interpersonal exchange, not of the text that carries it.

factors.definition: Content arrives in, or must be produced in, a form this person cannot perceive or operate, and the work of reaching it falls to them. The factor covers access to the channel, translation between forms with conflicting norms, and the independence in everyday life that access underwrites.
factors.boundary_rule: Concerns whether the person can reach and act on the material at all. F15 concerns tying content to a place, an object, or a movement. Nearest sibling: F15 (Spatial and Embodied Cognition).

sub_factors.definition: The exclusion of some people from an activity that is available to others, and the claim that removing that exclusion is what a design exists to do. Papers state a gap in participation — content that cannot be perceived, communication that cannot be conducted — and frame the inequality between those who can and cannot take part as the problem. Following the handoff's rule, this is coded only where access for the excluded group is the entire point of the design, not wherever such a group appears as participants.
sub_factors.framing: DEFICIT/HARM. Stated as inaccessibility, a communication gap, no choice, and aggravated inequality between disabled and non-disabled people.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: translating between forms with conflicting norms
sub_factors.definition: The person must re-express material in a second form whose conventions contradict the first form's, while keeping whatever made the original worth having. The claimed difficulty is that satisfying the target form's demands actively violates the source form's norms or the person's own training. It transplants to any conversion between representations with incompatible standards of what counts as good.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: independence and quality of life in daily living
sub_factors.definition: A person's ability to carry out the ordinary activities of their own life without depending on another person, and the standard of living that follows from it. Papers frame the target as relief from repeated manual effort in everyday tasks or as quality-of-life gains in daily and leisure activity. It transplants to any setting where the stake is a person conducting their own life rather than completing an assigned task.

factors.definition: The work depends on the person's body being where the work is, and on their ability to read a layout and picture arrangements and movements that are not in front of them. The difficulty is what is lost when the activity is done at a remove from the physical setting it concerns, or when spatial structure has to be held in the head.
factors.boundary_rule: Concerns bodily presence and spatial reasoning. F14 concerns whether the content reaches the person's senses at all. Nearest sibling: F14 (Accessibility).

sub_factors.definition: The person acts with their body and inside the physical setting the work concerns, and papers claim this bodily, in-place engagement is part of how the work gets done. The claimed deficit is separation: doing the work at a remove from the material context strips out information and felt continuity the person was relying on. It transplants to any activity whose decisions depend on being bodily present where the result will live.

A person has to understand how a place is laid out and to picture arrangements and movements within it that are not in front of them.
